<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918306_theRebbe_932" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918306_theRebbe_932__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar delivered on Shabbat Parshat Kedoshim, the second day of Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5736.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Kedoshim,</t>
    <t s="2">the second day of Rosh Chodesh Iyar, 5736*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the paradox of G-d having a throne and footstool, and resolves it by identifying heaven and earth with Torah and mitzvos, while the ultimate dwelling for Atzmus is through self-nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool,</t>
    <t s="1">which is the house that you will build for Me... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited..."1,</t>
    <t s="2">and the precise point in this is known2,</t>
    <t s="3">for He has no bodily form3</t>
    <t s="4">so how can it be said [He has] a throne and a footstool?</t>
    <t s="5">And also it must be understood what is meant by "which is the house that you will build for Me... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited,"</t>
    <t s="6">what is the virtue of the poor and broken-spirited,</t>
    <t s="7">for although "which is the house that you will build for Me,"</t>
    <t s="8">nevertheless "to this one"</t>
    <t s="9">(to the poor and broken-spirited)</t>
    <t s="10">"I will look."</t>
    <t s="11">And the point of the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="12">that heaven and earth are Torah and mitzvos</t>
    <t s="13">(as explained at length in Torah Or4),</t>
    <t s="14">which in general is the service of Nefesh HaElokis and Nefesh HaBahamis5.</t>
    <t s="15">And "house" is the service of "with all your might"6</t>
    <t s="16">which is above limitation7,</t>
    <t s="17">coming from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah5.</t>
    <t s="18">And the explanation of "which is the house that you will build for Me" is8,</t>
    <t s="19">that even the service that comes from the encompassing lights of Chayah and Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="20">through which the supernal encompassing lights are drawn down,</t>
    <t s="21">this is not "the house that you will build for Me"</t>
    <t s="22">("for Me" — for My Atzmus),</t>
    <t s="23">for even the most supreme encompassing lights are merely an illumination.</t>
    <t s="24">"To this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited"9,</t>
    <t s="25">for through self-nullification</t>
    <t s="26">(poor and broken-spirited)</t>
    <t s="27">there is a drawing down of Atzmus</t>
    <t s="28">("to this one I will look").</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the haftarah of "The heavens are My throne" to Shabbat Rosh Chodesh, explaining that the moon's nullification at its new moon allows it to receive a new light from above, paralleling the drawing down of Atzmus through self-nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that this is also the connection and relevance of the haftarah "The heavens are My throne" to Shabbat Rosh Chodesh,</t>
    <t s="3">for on Rosh Chodesh is the birth of the moon,</t>
    <t s="4">when then</t>
    <t s="5">(at the time of the new moon)</t>
    <t s="6">it is only a point,</t>
    <t s="7">which indicates its self-nullification10,</t>
    <t s="8">that it has nothing of its own at all11.</t>
    <t s="9">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="10">that in the moment just before the new moon it is in complete nullification,</t>
    <t s="11">that it is not even like a point,</t>
    <t s="12">and specifically through this its new moon is brought about12.</t>
    <t s="13">And through its self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="14">it receives a new light from the sun,</t>
    <t s="15">for the source of the drawing down of this light is not from the sun itself</t>
    <t s="16">(for there is nothing new under the sun13)</t>
    <t s="17">but from above14</t>
    <t s="18">from the Sun15.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is that on Shabbat Rosh Chodesh we read the haftarah "The heavens are My throne... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited...,"</t>
    <t s="20">for the drawing down that comes through self-nullification16</t>
    <t s="21">is a most exalted drawing down,</t>
    <t s="22">as explained above.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
